items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to establishing
the "New York state animal and plant fiber program"
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3396                Revised 2/11/2021

SPONSOR: MAY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to estab-
lishing the "New York state animal and plant fiber program"

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to expand the state's existing Grown and
Certified Program to include animal and plant fiber, such as sheep's
wool and hemp, as a new category of product eligible for such seal of
certification.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

The agriculture and markets law is amended by adding a new article 25-c
named New York State Animal and Plant Fiber Program and the commissioner
is directed to create such program within the New York Grown and Certi-
fied Program. The program will give producers of animal and plant fibers
the opportunity to apply for permission to use the Grown and Certified
seal on labels, packaging and advertisements for the products. Animal
and plant fibers are defined as those used to create textile products
and include sheep's wool, llama and alpaca and goat fiber, as well as
plants such as cotton and hemp.

The commissioner is authorized to promulgate rules and regulations
necessary to establish the program. The department will create educa-
tional materials and make them available on their website and distribute
same to Cornell Cooperative Extensions, Boards of cooperative educa-
tional services4-H development groups, organizers of county fairs, and
any other farming advocacy group deemed appropriate.  The animal and
plant fiber program would be introduced by the department at the upcom-
ing state fair.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

New York is uniquely positioned as one of only two states in the country
where it is possible to build a full scale and commercially viable farm-
to-fabric supply chain, and our textile manufacturers are eager to show-
case their high-quality products. The Grown and Certified Program has
helped elevate the market opportunities and consumer appeal for many New
York products ranging from cheese, to maple products, to beverages and
even Christmas trees and cut flowers. While consumers increasingly value
the opportunity to purchase local products, the Grown and Certified
Program has not yet offered its seal of exceptional quality to products
made of the fiber of animals or plants, such as sheep's wool clothing or
hemp-derived textiles. The boom in industrial hemp and the growing
interest in sheep and alpaca farming are trends we should reward and
encourage, and the new opportunity this bill affords textile producers
will also enhance connections between New York growers, processors, and
producers of finished items.

By expanding the Grown and Certified Program to animal and plant fiber
producers, New York will be able to showcase the exceptional quality of
this category of home-grown products and further boost its own agribusi-
ness entrepreneurs.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
90 days after enactment

A.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to establishing
the "New York state animal and plant fiber program"
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3396A

SPONSOR: MAY
 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this bill is to expand the state's existing Grown and
Certified Program to include animal and plant fiber, such as sheep's
wool and hemp, as a new category of product eligible for such seal of
certification.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 16 of the agriculture and markets law is amended by adding a new
subdivision 2-g directing the department, in cooperation with the
department of economic development, to assist in the promotion, market-
ing and sale, both within and outside the state, animal and plant fiber
and products made from such fiber. The program will give producers of
animal and plant fibers the opportunity to apply for permission to use
the Grown and Certified seal on labels, packaging and advertisements for
the products. Animal fibers are defined as natural fibers that have
formed the covering, or fleece, of sheep or other hairy animals such as
goats or alpacas, shorn for the purpose of creating textile products.
Plant fibers means natural fibers that are obtained from plants like
hemp and are used to create textile products.  The department will also
develop educational materials about animal and plant fiber, especially
for young people, in cooperation with cooperative extension, boards of
cooperative educational services, local fairs, and the state fair.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Grown and Certified Program has helped elevate the market opportu-
nities and consumer appeal for many New York products ranging from
cheese, to maple products, to beverages and even Christmas trees and cut
flowers. The Program has not yet offered its seal of exceptional quality
to products made of the fiber of animals or plants, such as sheep's wool
clothing or hemp-derived textiles. By expanding the Grown and Certified
Program to these producers, New York will be able to showcase the excep-
tional quality of this category of product and further boost to its own
agribusiness entrepreneurs.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately

summary: Provides for the promotion of New York state animal and plant fiber and products made from such fiber.
title: Provides for the promotion of New York state animal and plant fiber
